claims.text: Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only where the trace contains at least 3 consecutive position fixes inside the arrival radius for the zone class. This pickup is STANDARD (trip_record.pickup_zone_class), so the radius is 50 m, yet the driver's own track never comes closer than 779.93 m to the pin across 98 fixes at 100% coverage and the derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count = 0. There is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the trace, let alone in the 15 minutes before the 08:09:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the $4.00 cancellation fee is refundable in full.

The 08:02:14 'arrived' event is a false marker under POL-NS-05. At that timestamp the driver's nearest recorded position in the whole trace is still 779.93 m from the pickup pin, more than the 300 m threshold, and the driver's speed set includes 50.6 km/h, i.e. still in motion on a road rather than holding at the kerb. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies directly: the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be referred as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Even on the most generous reading, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against a required minimum of 300 seconds for STANDARD, a shortfall of the full 300 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall dispositive whether or not the rider was present, and its only qualification - accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under limb (i) - is unavailable here: the trace shows run_count 0 and 0 in-geofence intervals, and the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so there is no present and populated advisory of an admissible type on which limb (i) could operate. I disclose that artifact's impairment (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and rely on it only for the absence it establishes, which is itself citable.

POL-NS-04 independently exonerates the rider on all three limbs. (a) The chat log shows the rider sent a locating message at 08:05:33 - 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' - which both names the block and states that the rider cannot see the vehicle. (b) The driver never posted any reply, so nothing was sent within 120 seconds or at any later point, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no in-app voice call was placed before termination. (c) The rider's track places the device on the pin - 122 qualifying fixes, min 5.57 m, max 24.92 m, all well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, at a recorded speed of 0.0 throughout. The rider was at the pickup point, contacted the driver and was met with silence; the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue this fee. That clause applies only where the driver was stationary for the required dwell at a point outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; this driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 779.93 m, roughly double the 400 m ceiling, so he was not at the wrong face of the venue - he was not at the venue. In any event registered_pickup_points is 1, so pin ambiguity under POL-NS-03(ii) is not available, and the rider named the block in chat, which under POL-NS-03(i) would strip compensation even if the clause applied.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here limb (b) and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 both fail and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 each direct a full refund, so there is no verified no-show to compensate. The rider should not be made to fund a payout for a driver who was 780 m away when he marked arrival.

This case is decidable and does not need escalation under POL-NS-09. There is no admissible contradiction between artifacts - the trip record and the trace agree on the arrival marker and the cancellation time, and the trace carries a rider track rather than omitting one. The rider's and driver's disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so trigger (c) does not fire; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so trigger (d) does not fire, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip either (3 terminations in 30 days across 96 completed trips is 3.1 percent, below both the absolute count of 4 and the 0.08 rate). Every deciding artifact here - the trace, the trip record, the chat log and the fare breakdown - carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence floor is not engaged and no limb (e) impairment attaches to the deciding fact.

The money is unambiguous and already out of the rider's pocket: the fare breakdown shows the $4.00 cancellation fee charged at 08:09:55, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, with every other line (base, distance, time, platform fee, surge, ERP) at zero. The full contested amount of $4.00 is therefore the figure to return to the filing party, and it reconciles with the fee schedule for STANDARD plus RYDE_X, so nothing in POL-NS-08(d) stands in the way.

claims.text: The platform's own trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-07-23T08:02:14+08:00, and it records the trip as terminated by the driver on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises. Limb (a) of POL-NS-01 is therefore satisfied on the face of the record, and the driver's account of the trip is recorded in the platform's own terms rather than asserted after the dispute was filed.

The sum charged is exactly the sum the fee schedule fixes for this trip and is not inflated. On trip_record's STANDARD pickup zone class and RYDE_X vehicle tier the fee_schedule produces SGD 4.00 on the zone-class dimension and SGD 4.00 on the vehicle-tier dimension, so the GREATER required by the schedule's resolution rule is SGD 4.00, and the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 reconciles to it with a stated difference of 0.00. There is accordingly no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d), the ledger artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the contested sum is SGD 4.00 and no more.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard is not engaged on this driver. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the threshold of 4, and 3 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 96 is 3.1 per cent, below the 0.08 rate limb; both limbs must hold and neither does, so compensation is not withheld on this ground and POL-NS-09(d) is not triggered by the driver's no-show history. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a different field from the trailing-30-day figure POL-NS-07 names, and under POL-GEN-01 it may not be substituted for it or used to build an adverse finding against the driver.

Any refund on this dispute is confined to the cancellation-fee line. POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line only is refunded and not any booking or platform fee that would have been charged on a completed trip, and this ledger shows total_charged of SGD 4.00 with platform_fee 0.00, base_fare 0.00, distance and time fares 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The rider's contested amount of SGD 4.00 is therefore the whole of the exposure and the whole of any remedy available on this record.

On the driver's side the two admissible records cannot both be true about arrival, and the conflict goes to arrival and dwell themselves. The trip_record shows a driver arrival at 08:02:14 followed by a recorded wait of 7.4 minutes, and the platform posted a system notice 'Your driver has arrived' at 08:02:15; the gps_trace, running 98 fixes over the whole window at a 10 second cadence with 100 per cent coverage and no gap, has its nearest fix 779.93 m from the pickup pin and no fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. The full contested amount of SGD 4.00 is returned to the rider, confined to the cancellation-fee line, and no driver compensation is paid.

The driver's first submission is correct that limbs (a) and (d) are met on the face of the trip record, but a fee needs all four limbs and two of them are broken.

POL-NS-05 independently confirms the marker is false: at the arrival timestamp the driver is 779.93 m out, and the trace shows speeds up to 50.6 km/h. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) requires the full refund, no compensation, and a false-arrival referral — which I have issued. POL-NS-06 reaches the same result on the arithmetic: a 300-second shortfall, and its limb (i) accumulation is unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); I name that impairment and rely on the artifact only for the absence it establishes. NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-NS-07 pays 80% of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; it is not. The anti-farming check does not trip (3 no-show terminations in 30 days over 96 completed trips, 3.1%, below both the count-of-4 and 0.08 rate limbs), but that is moot when there is no verified no-show.

ON THE DRIVER'S ESCALATION REQUEST. I reject it. The fee is therefore refunded, not held for review.

The rider's fare-integrity point is accepted: $4.00 is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), and the ledger reconciles to it with a stated difference of 0.00, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect stands in the way, and the refund is confined to the cancellation-fee line. The driver's attempt to build anything on driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is correctly abandoned — the lifetime counter is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-30-day field POL-NS-07 names.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding fact — the driver never entered the pickup geofence — is carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is not engaged.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the rider's claim is supported in full. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged at 08:09:55 is refunded to the rider; no driver compensation is payable. Figures used: cancellation fee SGD 4.00 (fare breakdown EV-FARE-00201); minimum dwell 300 s and arrival radius 50 m for a STANDARD pickup (trip record EV-TRIP-00201); driver's nearest approach 779.93 m with 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes (GPS trace EV-GPS-00201).

To the rider — why you win. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00201, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, 98 driver fixes, no gaps) never brings the driver closer than 779.93 m to the pickup pin at Blk 118 Rivervale Dr, against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m, and the derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and run_count 0. Under POL-NS-02 the driver never arrived, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable. The 08:02:14 'arrived' event is a false marker under POL-NS-05: at that timestamp the driver was 779.93 m away, far past the 300 m threshold, and the trace carries a 50.6 km/h speed reading, i.e. he was still in motion. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies directly: full refund, no compensation, and the false-arrival referral below. Independently, POL-NS-06: effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, and limb (i) cannot rescue the shortfall (run_count 0; the advisory EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no present and populated advisory exists that would let separate intervals be summed — your advocate disclosed this impairment and relied on the absence only, which is citable). POL-NS-04 also exonerates you on all three limbs: the 08:05:33 message 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' is a locating message, the driver never replied and placed no in-app call (in_app_calls is empty), and your device sat 5.57–24.92 m from the pin across 122 qualifying fixes, inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. The refund is confined to the cancellation-fee line: the fare breakdown (weight 1.0) shows total_charged SGD 4.00 with every other line at zero, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and SGD 4.00 is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee (SGD 4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

To the driver — why the charge falls. Your point that POL-NS-01 limb (a) is met on the face of the record is correct: the trip record does contain an 'arrived' event and does carry the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code. But POL-NS-01 is conjunctive; (b) fails because the trace places you outside the geofence throughout, and (c) fails because the dwell is zero. Your argument that the trip record's arrival event conflicts with the trace and requires escalation under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected: that limb fires only where no clause resolves the conflict, and POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) and POL-NS-02 (arrival geofence) resolve it directly. An arrival tap records only that the tap was made; POL-NS-01 limb (c) runs the waiting clock from GPS entry into the geofence, not from the tap. POL-NS-03 does not help either: your closest approach of 779.93 m is roughly double the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling, so this is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case, and registered_pickup_points is 1 so pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable. Your fee-reconciliation and refund-confinement points are accepted (SGD 4.00 reconciles; only the cancellation-fee line is in issue). Your anti-farming point is accepted: 3 terminations in 30 days across 96 completed trips is 3.1%, below both the absolute count of 4 and the 0.08 rate, so compensation is not withheld on that ground, and the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags was correctly not substituted for the trailing-30-day figure. No driver compensation is payable under POL-NS-07 because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 displace it.

Confidence and integrity: no POL-NS-08(a)–(d) impairment attaches to any deciding artifact — no clock skew, no trace gap, chat message count matches the trip record, and the fee reconciles. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, and the case does not escalate.

ledger.claim: Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only where the trace contains at least 3 consecutive position fixes inside the arrival radius for the zone class. This pickup is STANDARD (trip_record.pickup_zone_class), so the radius is 50 m, yet the driver's own track never comes closer than 779.93 m to the pin across 98 fixes at 100% coverage and the derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count = 0. There is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the trace, let alone in the 15 minutes before the 08:09:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the $4.00 cancellation fee is refundable in full.

The 08:02:14 'arrived' event is a false marker under POL-NS-05. At that timestamp the driver's nearest recorded position in the whole trace is still 779.93 m from the pickup pin, more than the 300 m threshold, and the driver's speed set includes 50.6 km/h, i.e. still in motion on a road rather than holding at the kerb. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies directly: the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be referred as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Even on the most generous reading, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against a required minimum of 300 seconds for STANDARD, a shortfall of the full 300 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall dispositive whether or not the rider was present, and its only qualification - accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under limb (i) - is unavailable here: the trace shows run_count 0 and 0 in-geofence intervals, and the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so there is no present and populated advisory of an admissible type on which limb (i) could operate. I disclose that artifact's impairment (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and rely on it only for the absence it establishes, which is itself citable.

POL-NS-04 independently exonerates the rider on all three limbs. (a) The chat log shows the rider sent a locating message at 08:05:33 - 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' - which both names the block and states that the rider cannot see the vehicle. (b) The driver never posted any reply, so nothing was sent within 120 seconds or at any later point, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no in-app voice call was placed before termination. (c) The rider's track places the device on the pin - 122 qualifying fixes, min 5.57 m, max 24.92 m, all well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, at a recorded speed of 0.0 throughout. The rider was at the pickup point, contacted the driver and was met with silence; the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue this fee. That clause applies only where the driver was stationary for the required dwell at a point outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; this driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 779.93 m, roughly double the 400 m ceiling, so he was not at the wrong face of the venue - he was not at the venue. In any event registered_pickup_points is 1, so pin ambiguity under POL-NS-03(ii) is not available, and the rider named the block in chat, which under POL-NS-03(i) would strip compensation even if the clause applied.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here limb (b) and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 both fail and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 each direct a full refund, so there is no verified no-show to compensate. The rider should not be made to fund a payout for a driver who was 780 m away when he marked arrival.

This case is decidable and does not need escalation under POL-NS-09. There is no admissible contradiction between artifacts - the trip record and the trace agree on the arrival marker and the cancellation time, and the trace carries a rider track rather than omitting one. The rider's and driver's disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so trigger (c) does not fire; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so trigger (d) does not fire, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip either (3 terminations in 30 days across 96 completed trips is 3.1 percent, below both the absolute count of 4 and the 0.08 rate). Every deciding artifact here - the trace, the trip record, the chat log and the fare breakdown - carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence floor is not engaged and no limb (e) impairment attaches to the deciding fact.

The money is unambiguous and already out of the rider's pocket: the fare breakdown shows the $4.00 cancellation fee charged at 08:09:55, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, with every other line (base, distance, time, platform fee, surge, ERP) at zero. The full contested amount of $4.00 is therefore the figure to return to the filing party, and it reconciles with the fee schedule for STANDARD plus RYDE_X, so nothing in POL-NS-08(d) stands in the way.

The platform's own trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-07-23T08:02:14+08:00, and it records the trip as terminated by the driver on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises. Limb (a) of POL-NS-01 is therefore satisfied on the face of the record, and the driver's account of the trip is recorded in the platform's own terms rather than asserted after the dispute was filed.

The sum charged is exactly the sum the fee schedule fixes for this trip and is not inflated. On trip_record's STANDARD pickup zone class and RYDE_X vehicle tier the fee_schedule produces SGD 4.00 on the zone-class dimension and SGD 4.00 on the vehicle-tier dimension, so the GREATER required by the schedule's resolution rule is SGD 4.00, and the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 reconciles to it with a stated difference of 0.00. There is accordingly no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d), the ledger artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the contested sum is SGD 4.00 and no more.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard is not engaged on this driver. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the threshold of 4, and 3 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 96 is 3.1 per cent, below the 0.08 rate limb; both limbs must hold and neither does, so compensation is not withheld on this ground and POL-NS-09(d) is not triggered by the driver's no-show history. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a different field from the trailing-30-day figure POL-NS-07 names, and under POL-GEN-01 it may not be substituted for it or used to build an adverse finding against the driver.

POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line only is refunded and not any booking or platform fee that would have been charged on a completed trip, and this ledger shows total_charged of SGD 4.00 with platform_fee 0.00, base_fare 0.00, distance and time fares 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The rider's contested amount of SGD 4.00 is therefore the whole of the exposure and the whole of any remedy available on this record.

On the driver's side the two admissible records cannot both be true about arrival, and the conflict goes to arrival and dwell themselves. The trip_record shows a driver arrival at 08:02:14 followed by a recorded wait of 7.4 minutes, and the platform posted a system notice 'Your driver has arrived' at 08:02:15; the gps_trace, running 98 fixes over the whole window at a 10 second cadence with 100 per cent coverage and no gap, has its nearest fix 779.93 m from the pickup pin and no fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. That is the direct conflict between admissible artifacts on arrival and dwell that POL-NS-09(b) contemplates, and the driver's submission is that the disputed SGD 4.00 should be held for a human reviewer under POL-NS-09 rather than refunded on the automated pipeline while the two records stand unreconciled.
